info.title: hydromart-digital events for the AI web
info.description:
HD-7. Events hydromart-digital sends out, as signed HTTPS POSTs from admin-service. The AI web is the only receiver of these (its ingress route, then n8n); n8n has no public route (Plan Eksekusi section 4).

Registering: a SUPER_ADMIN adds the receiver URL and the event names at /hq/webhooks. The URL must be public HTTPS (a private or internal address is refused, at registration and again before every send). The signing secret is shown once, when the endpoint is registered; keep it in the receiver env. A secret is 32 to 200 printable ASCII characters with no spaces (a generated one is 64 hex characters). Every endpoint has one, and every delivery is signed.

Who receives an event: only an endpoint that is active and subscribed at the moment admin-service takes the event gets a delivery for it. Nothing is queued for an endpoint registered later, or switched off at that moment, so there is no backfill; moving older applications into the AI web CRM is planned for Tahap 2 (the /waralaba data move, which needs the consent HD-8 stores). Switching an endpoint off stops its sends from the next sweep round (one already claimed by a running round can still go out, within 5 minutes); what it had queued waits, and goes out when it is switched back on.

Verifying a delivery, in this order: (1) read the raw body bytes and verify those, never a re-serialised copy (key order inside data is not stable); (2) refuse when X-Hydromart-Timestamp is missing or more than 300 seconds from your own clock; (3) compute sha256= plus the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with the secret, and compare it with X-Hydromart-Signature in constant time; refuse a mismatch; (4) only the timestamp and the body are signed, so after verifying take event, id and eventId from the body, never from the X-Hydromart-Event or X-Hydromart-Delivery headers; (5) dedupe on eventId; (6) answer 2xx within 10 seconds and do slow work afterwards.

Never processing an event twice: one event can arrive more than once (a retry after a slow answer, a replay from HQ weeks later). Keep processed eventIds for good, not for a window. Record the eventId in the same transaction that durably queues the work, and only then answer 2xx: a crash between the two would otherwise lose the event, and its replay would then be deduped away. A repeat is answered 2xx without doing the work again. Answer 2xx as well for a verified event you do not know or cannot use: anything else is retried with the identical body.

Retries: a failure is any answer other than 2xx, a redirect (never followed), no complete answer within 10 seconds (the whole response, body included), or a connection error. A failed delivery is tried again no earlier than 1, 5, 25, 125 and 625 minutes later (the sweep runs every 5 minutes and sends at most 20 a round); the 6th failed attempt makes it DEAD, about 13 hours after the first, and HQ can send it again from /hq/webhooks. Before that hop, the producer keeps its own outbox and keeps trying admin-service (no earlier than 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 minutes after each failed try, then about hourly; its sweep runs every 10 minutes), until admin-service takes the event: an outage delays an event, it does not lose it.

Rotating the secret: first make the receiver accept both the current and the next secret; then a SUPER_ADMIN replaces it with a PATCH of the endpoint through the API (the console has no rotate action yet); then the receiver drops the old secret a few minutes later. Every retry and every replay is signed with the secret current at the moment it is sent, so after the PATCH only a request already in flight (claimed by a running sweep, at most 5 minutes) can still carry the old one. Never rotate by deleting and re-registering the endpoint: deleting drops its queued deliveries, and events published in between reach nobody.

Compatibility: receivers ignore fields they do not know. A field may be added within version 1; removing or renaming one is a new contract version. The x-hydromart-delivery block repeats the numbers above for code to read.

The same signing applies to every event admin-service sends. delivery.delivered is for delivery partners, carries the recipient name, and is not part of this contract: the AI web endpoint must not subscribe to it.

post.summary: A calon mitra submitted a franchise application on /waralaba
post.description:
Raised once per application submitted from this release on, and delivered to each endpoint that is active and subscribed when admin-service takes it (see info.description). The first workflow it feeds is AI-5: notify HQ and Sales.

It carries no personal data. Name, phone number, GPS location and amounts stay in hydromart-digital, on the application detail page /hq/applications/detail?id=<applicationId> (HEAD_OFFICE, DIREKTUR and SUPER_ADMIN). Moving the contact data into the AI web CRM is Tahap 2, after the /waralaba consent is stored (HD-8).

parameters.name: X-Hydromart-Event
parameters.description: The event name. NOT signed: a copy of the body field event, for logs only. Route on the verified body.

parameters.name: X-Hydromart-Delivery
parameters.description: The delivery id. NOT signed: a copy of the body field id, for logs only. Read the verified body.

parameters.name: X-Hydromart-Timestamp
parameters.description: Unix time in seconds at which THIS attempt was sent. Part of the signed string.

parameters.name: X-Hydromart-Signature
parameters.description: sha256= followed by the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<X-Hydromart-Timestamp>.<raw body>", keyed with the endpoint secret.

2XX.description: Taken (or already taken: a repeated eventId). The delivery is marked DELIVERED.

default.description: Anything else is retried (see info.description), and DEAD after the 6th failed attempt.

post.summary: An order was placed (online checkout or counter sale)
post.description: Raised once per order, in the same database transaction that writes the order (HD-17 part B), and delivered like every event (see info.description). A counter sale is born COMPLETED, so its status here is COMPLETED and no order.status_changed follows for the creation itself. It carries no personal data: ids, the depot, the channel and statuses only (no customer id, name, phone or address). Events of one order can arrive out of order after retries: receivers order them by occurredAt, never by arrival.

post.summary: An order moved from one status to another
post.description: Raised for EVERY status change of an order (about five per order), in the same database transaction as the change, including a counter void (COMPLETED to VOIDED). Events of one order can arrive out of order after retries: order them by occurredAt, never by arrival. It carries no personal data: ids, the depot, the channel and statuses only (no customer id, name, phone or address).

post.summary: A depot stock line fell below its reorder point
post.description: Raised when the sellable stock (on hand minus units held by open orders) of a depot line crosses to AT OR BELOW its reorder point (the depot's minimum stock; 0 disables it): onHand <= reorderPoint. Edge-triggered: it fires on the crossing, not on every later drop. At most one event per depot line per WIB calendar day (the date is the last part of eventId): a second crossing the same day is deduped silently, by design, so the AI web hears of a line once a day however often it crosses. It carries no personal data.

post.summary: HQ turned a calon mitra draft into a depot
post.description: Raised when HQ ACTIVATES a depot draft that the CRM made (POST /depot/api/v1/ai/drafts/depots/from-crm), in the same database transaction that creates the depot. The depot is therefore real when this arrives. One event per depot, ever: the eventId is keyed by the depot, so any retry, replay or producer re-send is the same event. It carries ids and the depot code only, no personal data: prospectId and legacyApplicationId are the CRM's own ids, to be matched in the AI web.

id.description: The delivery id: one per receiver endpoint, the same on its retries and replays. Not the dedupe key.

eventId.description: franchise.application_submitted:<applicationId>. The same on every retry, replay and producer re-send: the dedupe key.

city.description: City of the proposed depot, as the applicant typed it (the form allows 100 characters as it counts them; do not reject on length). Show it as text, never as markup.

province.description: Province of the proposed depot, as the applicant typed it (same rule as city).

id.description: The delivery id: one per receiver endpoint, the same on its retries and replays. Not the dedupe key.

eventId.description: order.created:<orderId>. The same on every retry, replay and producer re-send: the dedupe key.

id.description: The delivery id: one per receiver endpoint, the same on its retries and replays. Not the dedupe key.

eventId.description: order.status_changed:<orderId>:<transitionId>. The transition id is unique per status change, so a status an order revisits is a different event. The same on every retry, replay and producer re-send: the dedupe key.

id.description: The delivery id: one per receiver endpoint, the same on its retries and replays. Not the dedupe key.

eventId.description: stock.low:<depotId>:<itemId>:<WIB date YYYY-MM-DD>. The same on every retry, replay and producer re-send: the dedupe key.

depotId.description: The depot that fulfils it; null for an order not yet assigned to one.

channel.description: WALK_IN is a counter sale; ONLINE is every other order.

status.description: An order status. The list may grow within version 1: treat an unknown value as a plain string.

depotId.description: The depot that fulfils it; null for an order not yet assigned to one.

channel.description: WALK_IN is a counter sale; ONLINE is every other order.

from.description: An order status. The list may grow within version 1: treat an unknown value as a plain string.

to.description: An order status. The list may grow within version 1: treat an unknown value as a plain string.

itemType.description: AIR, GALON, TUTUP, SEGEL or PRODUK.

productId.description: The catalog product, for a PRODUK line; otherwise null.

onHand.description: Sellable stock after the change (physical quantity minus units held by open orders).

reorderPoint.description: The line's minimum stock; the event fires when onHand is at or below it.

id.description: The delivery id: one per receiver endpoint, the same on its retries and replays. Not the dedupe key.

eventId.description: depot.onboarded:<depotId>. The same on every retry, replay and producer re-send: the dedupe key.

depotCode.description: The depot's short code, e.g. BKS-01.

prospectId.description: The CRM prospect the depot came from (the prospectId the draft was made with).

legacyApplicationId.description: The /waralaba application it came from, when there was one.

x-hydromart-delivery.description: The delivery rules of info.description as numbers. admin-service tests assert them against the code.

x-hydromart-internal-publish-example.description: Internal, not for receivers: the body depot-service POSTs to admin-service (POST webhooks/events, internal key) for this event. depot-service tests assert their request has this shape; admin-service tests validate it against the ingest DTO, so the two halves cannot drift apart.

x-hydromart-signature-test-vector.description: A receiver implementation must produce exactly this signature from these inputs. admin-service tests check the signature; depot-service tests check that the body carries the data depot-service sends.
